newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent down slightly, but downside limited.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent down slightly, but downside limited.

text.p: August Brent futures were steady to lower on Tuesday in late SIMEX trading as values dipped in line with residual selling on NYMEX following day-earlier news that Iraq oil sales took a step closer.
August Brent on SIMEX was last traded at $17.80 per barrel, two cents down from London. September traded at $17.86, level with the London settlement.
NYMEX August crude was last traded on ACCESS at $18.97, down two cents from New York, but firmer than the $18.93 earlier.

Both markets fell on Monday on news Iraq was closer to resuming oil sales. Brokers said some spill over selling undermined prices in Asia Tuesday, but the downside was now limited because the market was technically oversold.

United Nations coordinator in Baghdad, Staffan de Mistura, said Monday that discussions about the Iraq aid plan had been completed and it would be submitted to the U.N. secretary general for final approval by next Monday.
Iraq has said it wanted to complete the aid distribution plan before resuming oil sales. It can sell $2 billion worth over a six-month period.

Tom James, Asia Pacific manager for Credit Lyonnais Rouse, said "you could see a short term upside correction as players take some money out of the market", starting later on Tuesday ahead of the weekly API release.
He saw immediate support at $17.48 and resistance at $18.16.
